_meta.indication: Detectnet is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for use with positron emission tomography (PET) for localization of somatostatin receptor positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult patients.
_meta.receipt_date: Received January 3, 2020 (submit dates July 8, 2019 and January 3, 2020)

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, single-center, single-dose, single-arm, non-comparative study assessing imaging performance of Cu-64 dotatate PET by comparison of blinded PET reader results to a standard of truth (SOT).
pivotal_trials.population: 42 adult patients with prior history of pathologically confirmed NET or suspected NET and 21 healthy volunteers.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: subject-level sensitivity and specificity of Cu-64 dotatate PET for NET, assessed against a standard of truth (SOT).
pivotal_trials.result: All three blinded readers demonstrated success on the co-primary efficacy endpoints, with lower bounds of the 95% CI for PPA (sensitivity) exceeding 70% and NPA (specificity) exceeding 60%. PPA (sensitivity) was 91% for all three readers and NPA (specificity) ranged from 80 to 97%.

key_safety: Reported adverse reactions include nausea, vomiting, and flushing, each occurring at a rate of <2%. No deaths or other serious adverse events were reported in the safety database of 71 subjects from prospective Applicant trials plus 126 patients from the published literature.
target_moa: Copper Cu 64 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors (highest affinity for SSTR2); the somatostatin analog octreotate binds SSTRs, DOTA is the chelator, and Cu-64 is the positron emitter, so PET images indicate the presence and density of somatostatin receptors in tissues.
modality: Radiopharmaceutical (Cu-64 radiolabeled somatostatin analog peptide for PET imaging)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting or external consultation was needed for this NDA; not referred because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues.

summary.text: Detectnet was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA for a designated new molecular entity and reviewed under Priority review. It received Fast Track designation (December 19, 2018) and orphan drug designation (May 18, 2016) as a diagnostic for the management of NETs; because of the orphan designation, PREA pediatric requirements were not applicable. It was approved on the standard (non-accelerated) pathway.

citations.quote: New drug application (NDA) 213227 is a 505(b)(2) application for this designated new molecular entity (NME).
Under IND 131797, Fast Track designation was granted for this product on December 19, 2018.

On May 18, 2016, orphan drug designation was granted to Cu-64 dotatate as a diagnostic for the management of NETs. Therefore, Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) requirements are not applicable to this NDA.
